name: How Do Contractors Fix Driveway Damage From Tree Roots?

mainEntity.name: What driveway problems are caused by tree roots, and can a contractor fix them permanently?
mainEntity.text: What driveway problems are caused by tree roots, and can a contractor fix them permanently?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tree roots can create several driveway problems, including lifted slabs, cracked panels, separated joints, and uneven walking or driving surfaces. A contractor may be able to remove and replace the damaged sections, but the repair is only permanent if the root issue is also addressed. That can mean rerouting the driveway layout, using root barriers, adjusting panel sizes, or coordinating with arborist guidance where appropriate. In Los Angeles County, many properties have mature landscaping close to hardscape, so root-related movement is common. Homeowners should ask whether the contractor has a plan for the roots themselves, not just the concrete or paving. If the tree remains and the roots continue to grow toward the driveway, new damage may appear later. A durable solution should balance the health of the landscape with the need for a stable driveway surface. Without that planning, repeated repairs can become a cycle instead of a fix.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tree roots can lift slabs, create cracks, separate joints, and make the driveway uneven. A contractor can repair the damaged sections, but a permanent fix often requires root management, redesign, or replacing affected panels. If the tree stays in place, the underlying root pressure may return over time.
